info.title: Rapidata Leaderboard API
info.description: The API for the Rapidata Leaderboard service

post.summary:
Creates one run per leaderboard of the benchmark, each evaluating the same explicit list of
 matchup configurations.
post.description:
Answers 202 with one entry per created run and the seed they all share, so every leaderboard
 evaluates identical image pairs; a seed is generated when none is supplied. Hidden
 leaderboards and leaderboards excluded from the benchmark overall are left out. See
 POST /leaderboard/{leaderboardId}/runs/custom for how configurations are validated
 and resolved.

get.summary: Returns the share of a benchmark's votes falling in each demographic bucket.
get.description:
The same vote-level filters as the standings query apply. Every dimension closes with an
 unknown bucket for votes with no recorded value, and its shares sum to 1. Benchmarks
 without granular votes return a zero-vote, empty-dimension response.

parameters.name: logic
parameters.description: How to combine the field filters: "and" (default) requires every filter to match, "or" requires any of them to match.

get.summary:
Returns a page of the requested confidence zone of an A-vs-B matchup — the prompts A clearly
 wins, the coin flips, or the prompts B clearly wins.
get.description:
Each vote is weighted by the annotator's reliability; a prompt is placed by the Wilson score
 interval on A's win share and, within the requested zone, ordered most-confident first (coin
 flips by effective sample size). The same vote-level filters as the matrix query apply.
 Benchmarks without granular votes return an empty page.

parameters.description: The id of participant A (the reference side of the split).

parameters.description: Which confidence zone of the matchup to page through.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: The number of items per page.

parameters.name: logic
parameters.description: How to combine the field filters: "and" (default) requires every filter to match, "or" requires any of them to match.

get.summary:
Returns the standings over the whole filtered set alongside the standings recomputed for each
 tag on the benchmark.
get.description:
The same vote-level filters as the standings query apply, except a tag filter — tags are what
 the response is sliced by. Every tag is returned, across every taxonomy axis, so the whole
 grid comes from one request; which axes to render is the caller's choice. Segment items carry
 the id and the numbers only: the participants' names and model metadata are identical in every
 segment and are reported once in global, to be joined on by id.

post.summary: Starts an asynchronous computation of the benchmark's prompt embedding map.
post.description:
Restricted to platform staff. Computing a map is what decides whether a benchmark exposes one
 on the anonymous read route, so it is a curation call rather than a benchmark-owner capability
 — a benchmark's owner cannot trigger or re-trigger it.
 
 Returns a tracking id immediately; poll
 GET /benchmark/{benchmarkId}/prompt-embedding-map/status for progress. Responds with
 409 Conflict when no embedding provider is configured, or when a computation for this
 benchmark is already in flight. Any map already being served stays in place until the new one
 succeeds, so triggering a recomputation is safe.

parameters.name: benchmarkId
parameters.description: The benchmark whose prompts should be embedded.

get.summary: Returns the benchmark's prompt embedding map.
get.description:
Unpaged: the whole corpus arrives in one response because the plot needs every point at once.
 Tag strings are de-duplicated into a map-level tags vocabulary that each point indexes
 via tagIndices. Prompts without English text are not embedded, so promptCount can
 be lower than the benchmark's prompt total and the map is not a complete corpus listing.
 Responds with 204 No Content when no map has been computed yet.

parameters.name: benchmarkId
parameters.description: The benchmark whose prompt embedding map should be returned.

get.summary: Returns the state of the benchmark's most recent prompt embedding map computation.
get.description:
Restricted to platform staff, matching the action it reports on. Deliberately narrower than the
 map itself, which is readable by anyone who can read the benchmark: a failure reason carries the
 embedding provider's raw error text, so it must not reach benchmark owners or the public.
 
 A benchmark has exactly one map, and this reports its most recent computation whatever the
 state, so a failure is visible here rather than silently absent. Responds with 204 No Content
 when no computation has ever been triggered for this benchmark.

parameters.name: benchmarkId
parameters.description: The benchmark whose computation state should be returned.

get.summary:
Queries a benchmark's image matchups — a page of compared image pairs with how the responses
 split between them.
get.description:
An item is one image pair as one leaderboard saw it — a pair compared on several leaderboards
 comes back once per board. Filters use the prompt-ratings query's field set, applied to the
 votes a matchup is tallied from, plus four outcome fields accepted only as top-level
 and leaves: WinnerParticipantId/LooserParticipantId pick the side that
 won the whole matchup (a tie matches neither), and Responses/Extremeness
 select on the evidence the matchup carries — together a fair-coin sign test, so
 extremeness[gte]=1.96 with responses[gte]=5 keeps splits a coin flip would
 reproduce under 5% of the time. WinnerSigma is sigma signed from the winning
 side; sort by -winner_sigma to separate records the pooled data confirms from upsets.
 Matchups of leaderboards excluded from the benchmark overall are never returned.

parameters.name: useWeightedScoring
parameters.description: Whether to report each side's wins weighted by annotator reliability.

parameters.name: groupBy
parameters.description: What a compared image stands for; per participant, self-matchups leave the page.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: The number of items per page.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort fields. Prefix with - for descending order (e.g. -created_at).

parameters.name: logic
parameters.description: How to combine the field filters: "and" (default) requires every filter to match, "or" requires any of them to match.

get.summary: Queries the win matrix of a benchmark.
get.description:
Filters apply to the underlying votes. Benchmarks without granular vote storage evaluate
 only the filters their aggregated data can answer (tags, participants, leaderboards, runs,
 prompt identifiers); demographic and vote-time filters require granular vote storage.
 Alongside the matchup outcomes in data, each response also carries votes: the
 un-binarized human vote counts on the same axes, display-only and not reflected in scoring.

parameters.name: useWeightedScoring
parameters.description: Whether to apply weighted scoring based on user scores.

parameters.name: logic
parameters.description: How to combine the field filters: "and" (default) requires every filter to match, "or" requires any of them to match.

get.summary:
Queries a benchmark's prompt ratings — a page of prompts, each with its ranked entries and the
 pairwise win matrix over them.
get.description:
Filters apply to the underlying votes with the standings query's field set. A rating is an
 entry's standing against the other entries on its prompt, so a participant filter narrows the
 entries but does not refit, and a prompt with no matching votes yields no entries.
 groupBy decides what competes: per participant, a participant's images become one entry
 rated from their pooled wins, and comparisons between its own images are excluded from the
 rating, both matrices, and responseCount. Grouping never changes which prompts the page
 holds.

parameters.name: useWeightedScoring
parameters.description: Whether to weight ratings by annotator reliability.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: The number of items per page.

parameters.name: sort

parameters.name: logic
parameters.description: How to combine the field filters: "and" (default) requires every filter to match, "or" requires any of them to match.

post.summary:
Creates a run that evaluates an explicit list of matchup configurations, each with its own
 response count.
post.description:
Answers 202 once the configurations are validated and the run is queued; it then starts
 behind whatever else is queued on the leaderboard, and its matchups are resolved at that
 point. Poll GET /leaderboard/{leaderboardId}/runs for its status. Every id is
 verified before the 202, but a configuration that resolves to no matchups is only found at
 start and is skipped; the run fails when all of them do. At most 2000 configurations,
 1000000 responses and 10000 referenced ids per request.

parameters.name: leaderboardId
parameters.description: The id of the leaderboard to run the matchups on.

requestBody.description: The run name and the matchup configurations to evaluate.

post.summary: Rebalances a leaderboard by adding responses for the given participants.
post.description:
Unlike the plain boost, which only generates matchups among the boosted participants,
 this matches each given participant evenly against every other participant of the
 benchmark — the same distribution a participant receives when it is first submitted.
 Use it to bring under-sampled participants up to the rest of the leaderboard.

 benchmark's already-submitted field — where the same participants submitted one by one would
 be compared in submission order. All participants must belong to the same benchmark, be
 ready for evaluation, and appear at most once; at most 100 per request.

post.summary: Re-queues failed items of a sample generation so they run again.
post.description:
When no item ids are supplied, every failed item of the generation qualifies. Item ids that
 do not belong to the generation or are not in a failed state are ignored. Returns the ids
 that were re-queued; a generation with no failed items yields an empty result.
 When no failure categories are supplied, the retry covers only the items whose failure a
 re-run can plausibly fix, so items rejected for the request itself — an unknown model,
 refused credentials, a content-policy or configuration rejection — are left alone rather than
 re-run to collect the same rejection. Naming those categories explicitly retries them anyway;
 combining categories with item ids intersects the two.

seed.description:
Optional seed for deterministic matchup selection. Reuse it across a benchmark's leaderboards to align them on the same
 image pairs; omit for random selection.

itemIds.description:
The specific item ids to retry. When omitted or empty, every failed item of the
 generation qualifies.

failureCategories.description:
The failure categories to retry. When omitted or empty, only the categories a re-run can
 plausibly fix qualify. Combined with item ids the two intersect.

retriedCount.description: How many failed items were re-queued.

retriedItemIds.description: The ids of the items that were re-queued.

models.description: The matching models for this page.

nextCursor.description: Cursor to fetch the next page, or null when there are no more results.

repoName.description:

 defaults to a name derived from the benchmark name.

fullRebuild.description: When true, re-export the entire benchmark as a non-incremental sync. Defaults to false.

status.description: Current lifecycle status (NeverSynced when the benchmark has never been synced).

voteAggregation.description:
How votes on a matchup aggregate into the stored result: AllVotes counts every vote as a matchup,
 MajorityVote collapses each to a single majority win (ties split 0.5/0.5). Only affects future runs.

 another tag is included.
